facts.statement: Drusilasaura was an extinct genus of titanosaur sauropod dinosaur that may belong to the group Lognkosauria.
facts.quote: Drusilasaura is an extinct genus of possible lognkosaurian titanosaur sauropod dinosaur

facts.statement: Drusilasaura lived during the late Cretaceous, specifically the Cenomanian to Turonian stages, in Santa Cruz Province, southern Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: which lived during the late Cretaceous (Cenomanian-Turonian stage) of Santa Cruz Province of southern Patagonia, Argentina

facts.statement: The fossil remains of Drusilasaura were discovered by paleontologist Marcelo Tejedor while searching for fossil mammals in the Upper Member of the Bajo Barreal Formation on the María Aike Ranch.
facts.quote: It was found by palaeontologist Marcelo Tejedor searching fossil mammals, in layers of the Upper Member of the Bajo Barreal Formation, on the María Aike Ranch owned by the Ortiz de Zárate family

facts.statement: The genus Drusilasaura was named by César Navarrete, Gabriel Casal, and Rubén Martínez in 2011.
facts.quote: Drusilasaura was named by César Navarrete, Gabriel Casal and Rubén Martínez in 2011

facts.statement: The generic name Drusilasaura honors Drusila Ortiz de Zárate, a young woman who owned the ranch where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The generic name honours Drusila Ortiz de Zárate, a young female member of the family who owns the ranch where the fossil was found

facts.statement: The specific name deseadensis refers to the Río Deseado.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to the Río Deseado

facts.statement: Drusilasaura was a large sauropod with a scapula measuring 143 cm, which is 30% longer than that of Mendozasaurus.
facts.quote: Drusilasaura is a large sauropod. The length of the scapula is 143 cm, 30% longer than that of Mendozasaurus

facts.statement: Describers assigned Drusilasaura to the family Titanosauridae and considered it a possible member of the clade Lognkosauria.
facts.quote: Drusilasaura was assigned to the Titanosauridae by the describers and considered a possible member of the Lognkosauria

facts.statement: If Drusilasaura is indeed a member of Lognkosauria, it would be the oldest known member of that group.
facts.quote: If so, it would be the oldest known lognkosaurian

facts.statement: Drusilasaura lived between 100.5 and 89.8 million years ago during the Cenomanian to Turonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Turonian (100.5 to 89.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group for Drusilasaura is Lognkosauria.
Drusilasaura belongs to the class Saurischia.
